newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey opens up gold market to overseas firms.
newsitem.headline: Turkey opens up gold market to overseas firms.

text.p: Turkey has introduced new regulations to open the Istanbul gold exchange to finance houses and overseas firms, the official gazette said on Tuesday.

"The new regulations aim to draw idle gold estimated at around $73 billion into the Turkish economy and give the Exchange an international character," Kaan Rasim Aytogu, general secretary of the Istanbul gold exchange and advisor to the Prime Minister, told Reuters.

The new regulations allow finance houses and foreign traders and institutions to become members of the gold exchange, besides local banks, brokerage houses, foreign exchange offices and precious metals trading companies.
Aytogu said Turkey aimed to attract bullion and dealers mainly from the Central Asian republics of Uzbekistan, Kazakhistan and Kyrgyzstan to Istanbul.
"The changes aim to draw gold produced in the Central Asian states, namely Uzbekistan, Kazakhastan and Kyrgyzstan, to Istanbul and through Istanbul to international markets," he added.
He said the exchange had already received several membership applications from the three Central Asian states.
The exchange currently has 54 members, including 25 banks. Six finance houses, known as Islamic banks, operate in Turkey on a revenue-sharing basis.
New applications will be handled by the Treasury.
Aytogu said a reform package to activate gold trade in Turkey would be completed with the launch of a futures and options market as well as a planned refinery in Istanbul.

He said a final regulation was awaited for futures and options to be launched on the gold exchange. Some 39 intermediaries have so far been approved by the regulatory Capital Markets Board to trade on the foreign exchange and gold futures and options market.
"A decree prepared by the Finance Ministry to exempt futures and options deals from stamp tax is at the final phase of being signed by the cabinet," Aytogu said.
"A regulation on the structuring of the planned gold refinery has been completed and submitted for approval to the Prime Ministry," he added.
Aytogu said the two final regulations would allow gold certificates to be launched as a capital market instrument by financial intermediaries in return for idle gold to be brought to the refinery.
Turkey had the world's third biggest gold trading volume after Italy and India with 253 tonnes in 1996. About 220 tonnes of gold worth $2.6 billion was imported in the same period.
